trans.sense: those with chief in their business titles

examples.text: THE customer is king. So some firms have started appointing chief customer officers (CCOs) to serve the king more attentively. These new additions to the (already crowded) C-suite are supposed to look at the business from the customer’s point of view.
examples.ref: 2012 September 22, “Schumpeter: The magic of good service”, in The Economist:

raw_glosses: (management) The group of officers of a business organization who have the word chief in their titles.
glosses: The group of officers of a business organization who have the word chief in their titles.

raw_glosses: (management) Senior headquarters executives: the chiefs and their immediate subordinates.
